problem: Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=1+{e}^{\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Arc Length of a Polar Curve

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14077889/assets/1bd01b4fe70a497cc66811a2d5b070908221b9932655ee396d9a8039471702c2.png)

Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \pi $ (shown in blue in the diagram above)?
feedback.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{5+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
